scope: Provisional ID agentic benchmarks only. This queue selects new authoring work; it does not change benchmark coverage states.

selection_policy.primary: Prioritize feasible, missing BixBench-Verified-50 endpoints for the MVP, then other ID benchmark-derived competencies. Require independent observed inputs and complete executable acceptance; use the provisional scientific taxonomy as a diversity check, not a fixed allocation.
selection_policy.deduplication: Deduplicate authored task/input hashes and biological lineages. Retain benchmark aliases as provenance only.
selection_policy.counting: A shared tool, component mapping, broad family label or uninspected identifier contributes no completed-task credit. Conditional candidate counts are upper bounds until all data and endpoint requirements pass.
constraints: Observed independent biological inputs; no benchmark fixtures or answers.
A coherent scientific task, offline by default, target at most 30 minutes. Scale recipes only through meaningful independent data or decisions.
Input-reading oracle and complete deterministic artifact checks; no teacher model API calls or LLM judge for generation or grading.
Preserve every OOD assignment; do not inspect OOD tasks for authoring.
tiebreakers: Feasible source data and deterministic assessment within the least-served branch.
Additional independent biological lineages and meaningful scientific decisions.
Lower incremental authoring and validation cost.
selection_policy.secondary: Repository, format and operation coverage support the chosen competencies; package use alone earns no competency credit.
selection_policy.refresh: After each accepted or rejected task, reassess missing benchmark-derived operations and scientific decisions. Keep exact evidence and partial mappings; no new taxonomy or weighted quota is adopted.
selection_policy.scope_limit: Current taxonomy and allocation illustrations are provisional; paper counts and demand weights remain undecided.

authoring_policy.unit: One complete Harbor task per author
owner_responsibilities: Specify the scientific question and eligible benchmark-derived competency

authoring_policy.integration_owner: Review shared interfaces and task integration, resolve conflicting edits, approve evidence claims, commit and publish
authoring_policy.execution_policy: Assign one complete Harbor task per owner and keep current owners productive. Choose concurrency according to available agent slots and measured node load and memory. Three owners are currently assigned, not a hard cap. Serialize intensive local commands with the nonblocking shared lock; run native scientific checks on authorized reserved TRC CPU capacity subject to Iris scheduling. Avoid large local downloads and reduce work when measured contention requires it.
authoring_policy.authorization: User authorized parallel complete-task owners and removed the node-wide fixed child-agent cap on 2026-09-25. Preserve this authorization across compaction. Resource monitoring and serialized intensive local commands remain required.

current_objective: Produce reusable, realistic computational-biology Harbor tasks with private native-package oracles, complete executable artifact checks and public inspection. Derive competencies from provisional ID agentic benchmarks; preserve all OOD exclusions. Prefer observed biological data and connected workflows, one meaningful task per recipe and one train split, with no count cap. Taxonomy and allocation weights remain provisional. Model training, teacher traces, model choice and context budgets are outside this task-generation scope.
